processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The experimental steel Fe-0.25C-3Mn-2Al-0.4Si (mass fraction) was melted in a vacuum induction furnace.
After melting the steel was hot forged.

processing_steps.method: austenitization / soaking prior to hot rolling
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Specimens were heated to 1200 °C and held for 60 min before hot rolling.

processing_steps.method: six-pass hot rolling on a φ350 mm × 350 mm high-stiffness two-high hot rolling mill
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Six-pass rolling; initial rolling temperature 1100 °C, final rolling temperature 880 °C, cumulative reduction ratio 90 %.

processing_steps.method: cold rolling on a four-high reversible cold rolling mill
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cold rolling experiment with a total reduction ratio of 60 % performed on a four-high reversible cold rolling mill.
The cold-rolled specimen was annealed at 800 °C for 30 min, then air cooled to room temperature. This is the step that produces the ANT800 specimen (vs ANT750/ANT850).
After annealing the specimen was held at 400 °C for 30 min and air cooled, completing the ANT800 thermal schedule.

structures.overall_structure: Dual-phase ferrite + bainite microstructure (with retained austenite < 5 %) of the air-cooled Fe-0.25C-3Mn-2Al-0.4Si steel annealed at 800 °C for 30 min.

phases_present.morphology: bright, rough-etched network (denser, more continuous in AN800)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: ferrite 5.4 μm (43 vol%), bainite 4.1 μm (55.1 vol%)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Instron 3382 universal electronic materials testing machine; air-cooled specimens; three samples tested per group to ensure reliability/repeatability

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve of the 800 °C annealed specimen (red curve) in Fig. 12: peaks just above 1200 MPa at roughly 5 % strain and ends near 13 % strain.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Strengthening-mechanism contributions calculated/derived for the ANT800 specimen (σ_YS = σ0 + σg + σd + σOrowan); values reported in Table 3.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: YS prediction difference at 800 °C: plain Extra Trees 31 MPa vs GA-Extra Trees 10 MPa (reduction of 21 MPa). GA-Extra Trees predicted 978 MPa vs measured 968 MPa; plain Extra Trees predicted 999 MPa.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ETD detector, 20.00 kV, spot 5.9, mode Custom, magnification 3,000×, WD 10.7 mm, 40 µm scale bar
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room-temperature SEM of the annealed specimen surface
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the ferrite/bainite morphology of the AN800 specimen
characterization_methods.key_findings: AN800 shows a markedly denser, more continuous bright bainite network enclosing smaller dark ferrite areas compared with AN750.

characterization_methods.technique: Image analysis with Image-Pro Plus software
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Several SEM images per specimen; average values calculated
characterization_methods.purpose: Statistical analysis of ferrite grain size and volume fraction
characterization_methods.key_findings: For AN800 the ferrite volume fraction is 43 % with average grain size 5.4 μm; bainite fraction 55.1 % with average grain size 4.1 μm.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EBSD with scanning step size 0.2 μm
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Local orientation difference (average KAM) used to compute GND density
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine geometrically necessary dislocation density and Taylor factor
characterization_methods.key_findings: AN800: GND density 0.84×10^14 m^-2 and Taylor factor 3.58 (highest of the three specimens).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Instron 3382 universal electronic materials testing machine
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature; strain rate 5 × 10^-4 s^-1; gauge 15 mm × 5.0 mm × 1.0 mm; three samples per group
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure yield strength and plot engineering stress-strain curves at different annealing temperatures
characterization_methods.key_findings: ANT800 (800 °C) measured YS = 968 MPa; the 800 °C curve peaks just above 1200 MPa and ends near 13 % strain.

computational_details.simulation_method: Analytical strengthening-mechanism calculations (linear superposition model σ_YS = σ0 + σg + σd + σOrowan)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Inputs: chemical composition of Fe-0.25C-3Mn-2Al-0.4Si, measured ferrite/bainite grain size and volume fraction, and GND density/Taylor factor of the AN800 specimen.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Theoretical σy = 935 MPa vs measured YS = 968 MPa for AN800 (model overestimates by 33 MPa).

analytical_models.model_note: Δσ0 = 32.3[Mn] + 83.2[Si] + 360[C] + 354.2[N] + 11[Mo] − 30[Cr]; friction stress included; result for the test steel is 220 MPa (same for AN750/AN800/AN850).

analytical_models.equation_role: Compute grain-boundary strengthening σg via mixing rule
analytical_models.model_note: σg = Kd^-1/2 with σg = f_α σ_α + f_β σ_β; result for AN800 is σg = 256 MPa.

analytical_models.equation_role: Compute dislocation contribution σd from GND density
analytical_models.model_note: σd = αMGbΔρ^1/2 with ρ_GND = 2θ/(μb); result for AN800 is σd = 459 MPa.

computational_details.simulation_method: GA-optimized Extremely Randomized Trees (GA-Extra Trees) regression for yield-strength prediction
computational_details.software_used: Python; DEAP 1.3.3 framework for the GA hyper-parameter search
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: GMM-augmented dataset (776 entries, from 177 original literature data) plus the six strengthening-mechanism features
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Input features: σ0, σg, σd, σOrowan contributions of the ANT800 specimen; output: YS. GA settings: search over six hyper-parameters, population size 30, crossover 0.7, mutation 0.3, convergence after the 26th of 30 generations. Optimised hyper-parameters (Table 2): n_estimators=1657, max_depth=51, min_samples_split=3, min_samples_leaf=1.0, max_features=0.85, max_samples=0.92.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: For ANT800 (800 °C): GA-Extra Trees predicted 978 MPa vs measured 968 MPa (difference 10 MPa); plain Extra Trees predicted 999 MPa (difference 31 MPa).

unmapped_findings: Strengthening-mechanism contributions for the AN800 (ANT800) specimen (Table 3): σ0 = 220 MPa (solid solution, incl. matrix friction stress), σg = 256 MPa (grain refinement), σd = 459 MPa (dislocation), σOrowan = 0 MPa (Orowan), giving theoretical σy = 935 MPa versus the measured YS = 968 MPa.

The Orowan strengthening contribution is 0 MPa for the Fe-0.25C-3Mn-2Al-0.4Si steel because the Al and Si additions suppress carbide formation, so no significant precipitation occurs; this holds for the whole test steel including AN800.

The Taylor factor of the AN800 specimen is 3.58 (the highest among AN750/AN800/AN850), alongside a GND density of 0.84×10^14 m^-2; AN800 reaches both the highest mean GND density and highest mean Taylor factor, giving it the largest dislocation-strengthening contribution.
Retained austenite in the annealed specimens is < 5 % and its strengthening contribution was neglected.
Across the three annealing conditions (750-850 °C) of the Fe-3Mn-2Al-0.25C-0.4Si alloy, the average error between predicted and measured YS was 1.56 %; this figure is not specific to ANT800 alone.
